fed.name: US Federal Reserve policy rate
fed.desc: The overnight rate set by the US Fed. It anchors global borrowing costs and the dollar.

us10y.name: US 10-year Treasury yield
us10y.desc: The world's benchmark long-term interest rate.

realyield.name: US real yields (10Y TIPS)
realyield.desc: Interest rates after inflation. The opportunity cost of holding gold and long-duration assets.

dxy.name: US dollar
dxy.desc: The dollar against major currencies. A strong dollar tightens global financial conditions.

us_inflation.name: US inflation
us_inflation.desc: Consumer price inflation in the US; drives Fed policy.

us_growth.name: US economic growth
us_growth.desc: Activity in the world's largest economy: jobs, spending, earnings.

china_growth.name: China growth & stimulus
china_growth.desc: The largest buyer of most commodities; stimulus lifts metals demand.

global_liquidity.name: Global liquidity (Fed balance sheet)
global_liquidity.desc: Money created by central banks. More liquidity tends to lift risk assets.

risk_appetite.name: Global risk appetite (VIX)
risk_appetite.desc: Investor fear gauge. A higher VIX means less appetite for risky assets, and is shown inverted in links.

geopolitics.name: Geopolitics & conflicts
geopolitics.desc: Wars, sanctions and shipping disruptions. They raise risk premiums on oil and gold.

opec.name: OPEC+ supply decisions
opec.desc: Production quotas from oil exporters; the biggest swing factor for crude supply.

central_bank_gold.name: Central-bank gold buying
central_bank_gold.desc: Reserve diversification by central banks (China, India, Poland, Turkey) away from the dollar.

ai_capex.name: AI & data-centre investment
ai_capex.desc: Spending on chips, servers and power by large tech firms.

us_tech.name: US tech stocks
us_tech.desc: Nasdaq 100: sets global tech valuations and sentiment for Indian IT.

us_equities.name: US equities
us_equities.desc: S&P 500, the anchor for global equity sentiment.

em_equities.name: Emerging-market equities
em_equities.desc: Where India competes for foreign portfolio money.

bitcoin.name: Bitcoin
bitcoin.desc: The largest crypto asset; trades as a liquidity-sensitive risk asset.

rbi.name: RBI repo rate & liquidity
rbi.desc: The Reserve Bank of India's policy rate and system liquidity (T-bill rate shown).

india_10y.name: India 10-year G-sec yield
india_10y.desc: India's benchmark borrowing cost; drives home-loan and corporate rates.

india_bonds.name: India government bond prices
india_bonds.desc: Long gilt prices move opposite to yields.

india_cpi.name: India inflation (CPI)
india_cpi.desc: Consumer inflation; RBI targets 4%. Food and fuel are the swing items.

india_growth.name: India GDP & corporate earnings growth
india_growth.desc: The base for Indian equity returns over time.

govt_capex.name: Government capital spending
govt_capex.desc: Union & state spending on roads, rail, defence and power. Drives order books.

fiscal.name: Fiscal deficit & subsidies
fiscal.desc: Government borrowing; higher deficits push bond yields up.

monsoon.name: Monsoon rainfall
monsoon.desc: Sets farm output, rural incomes and food prices for the year.

rural_demand.name: Rural demand
rural_demand.desc: Spending by ~65% of India's population; tied to crops, wages and MSP.

urban_demand.name: Urban consumption
urban_demand.desc: Spending on discretionary goods, travel, eating out; tied to jobs and wages.

housing.name: Housing & real-estate activity
housing.desc: New launches, sales and registrations; feeds cement, steel, paints, pipes, furnishings.

credit_growth.name: Bank credit growth
credit_growth.desc: Loan growth across retail, MSME and corporates.

festive.name: Festive & wedding season
festive.desc: Oct–Dec spending peak for autos, jewellery, durables and apparel.

power_demand.name: Electricity demand
power_demand.desc: Peak power demand; driven by heat waves, industry and data centres.

usdinr.name: US dollar / Indian rupee
usdinr.desc: Rupees per dollar. Up = weaker rupee: helps exporters, hurts importers.

fpi.name: Foreign portfolio flows into India
fpi.desc: Net buying by foreign investors (NSDL). Big swing driver for large caps and the rupee.

dii.name: Domestic institutional & SIP flows
dii.desc: Monthly SIPs and insurance money: a steady domestic buyer.

nifty.name: Nifty 50
nifty.desc: India's benchmark index; captures overall market moves (beta).

india_vix.name: India VIX
india_vix.desc: Expected Nifty volatility; spikes during sell-offs.

regulation.name: Regulation & policy changes
regulation.desc: SEBI, RBI, tariff and tax decisions that change sector economics.

gst.name: GST & indirect taxes
gst.desc: Rate changes alter final prices and demand.

pli.name: Production-linked incentives (PLI)
pli.desc: Subsidies for domestic manufacturing (electronics, solar, pharma inputs, autos).

tariffs.name: Global trade tariffs
tariffs.desc: Import duties by the US and others on Indian goods (textiles, gems, chemicals, auto parts).

brent.name: Crude oil (Brent)
brent.desc: The global oil benchmark; India imports ~85% of its crude.

natgas.name: Natural gas / LNG
natgas.desc: Fuel for power, fertiliser and city gas; India imports ~half its gas as LNG.

coal.name: Coal prices
coal.desc: Thermal coal for power and coking coal for steel.

gold.name: Gold
gold.desc: The global safe-haven and reserve asset.

silver.name: Silver
silver.desc: Half precious metal, half industrial (solar, electronics).

copper.name: Copper
copper.desc: Industrial bellwether: wiring, power grids, EVs, data centres.

aluminium.name: Aluminium
aluminium.desc: Packaging, autos, power lines; energy-intensive to produce.

steel.name: Steel (HRC)
steel.desc: Hot-rolled coil prices; India's steelmakers price off global and import parity.

tio2.name: Titanium dioxide
tio2.desc: White pigment used in paints and plastics.

palm_oil.name: Edible oils (palm, soy)
palm_oil.desc: Key input for soaps, foods and snacks; India imports most of it.

wheat.name: Wheat & grains
wheat.desc: Input for flour, biscuits and food prices.

sugar.name: Sugar
sugar.desc: Global sugar price; drives Indian mill realisations and ethanol economics.

fertiliser_inputs.name: Fertiliser inputs (ammonia, phosphate)
fertiliser_inputs.desc: Imported raw materials for urea/DAP makers.

chemicals_china.name: China chemical prices & dumping
chemicals_china.desc: Chinese oversupply sets global prices for many specialty chemicals.

construction_cost.name: Construction & finishing costs
construction_cost.desc: Cost of building and finishing homes, offices and infrastructure.

home_affordability.name: Home affordability
home_affordability.desc: Price and EMI burden for home buyers.

food_inflation.name: Food inflation
food_inflation.desc: Prices of cereals, vegetables, edible oils, milk; ~45% of India's CPI.

fuel_prices.name: Petrol, diesel & LPG prices
fuel_prices.desc: Retail fuel prices; partly set by government and oil marketers.

transport_cost.name: Freight & logistics costs
transport_cost.desc: Trucking, shipping and air-freight costs across the economy.

electricity_tariff.name: Electricity tariffs
electricity_tariff.desc: Power prices for homes and industry.

trade_deficit.name: India trade & current-account deficit
trade_deficit.desc: Import bill minus exports; oil and gold are the largest imports.

jobs_wages.name: Jobs & wages
jobs_wages.desc: Hiring and salary growth (IT, banking and manufacturing are big employers).

consumer_wallet.name: Household spending power
consumer_wallet.desc: What households have left after essentials and EMIs.

vehicle_cost.name: Vehicle prices & running costs
vehicle_cost.desc: Sticker prices and fuel/tyre costs of owning vehicles.

farm_income.name: Farm incomes
farm_income.desc: Crop output × prices; drives rural demand.

bank_asset_quality.name: Bank loan quality (NPAs)
bank_asset_quality.desc: Share of loans at risk of default.

savings_shift.name: Household savings shift to markets
savings_shift.desc: Money moving from deposits/gold into mutual funds and stocks.

gold_loans.name: Gold-loan collateral value
gold_loans.desc: Value of gold pledged against loans.

infra_buildout.name: Infrastructure build-out
infra_buildout.desc: Roads, rail, ports, power and urban projects.

telecom_tariffs.name: Mobile tariffs & data costs
telecom_tariffs.desc: Prices paid for mobile and broadband.

healthcare_cost.name: Healthcare costs
healthcare_cost.desc: Prices of medicines and hospital care.

digital_adoption.name: Digital & AI adoption by companies
digital_adoption.desc: Corporate spending on software, cloud and AI.

packaging_cost.name: Packaging costs
packaging_cost.desc: Cost of plastic, paper, glass and aluminium packaging for consumer goods.

edges: Higher inflation pushes the Fed to keep rates high.
Real yield = nominal yield minus inflation expectations.
Higher US rates attract capital to the dollar.
Abundant liquidity lifts appetite for risk (lower VIX).
Rate hikes and balance-sheet shrinkage drain liquidity.
A strong dollar tightens conditions for emerging markets.
When the dollar strengthens globally, the rupee usually weakens.
Higher discount rates hit long-duration growth stocks.
AI spending drives earnings of chipmakers and cloud firms.
Bitcoin trades as a liquidity-sensitive asset.
A weaker dollar has tended to support crypto.
Gold pays no interest; higher real yields raise the cost of holding it.
Gold is priced in dollars; a strong dollar makes it costlier elsewhere.
Central banks have bought ~1,000 t a year since 2022.
Fear (high VIX) can lift gold as a hedge.
Silver tracks gold with higher volatility.
Higher prices cut volumes but lift value per gram.
Higher gold prices raise collateral values and loan sizes.
More supply lowers prices; cuts raise them.
China is the largest crude importer.
Middle East and Russia risks add a supply premium.
Dollar-priced commodities fall when the dollar rises.
Retail fuel follows crude with policy lags.
Oil is India's largest import (~25% of the bill).
A higher oil bill weakens the rupee.
Fuel, transport and petrochemical costs feed inflation.
Diesel is the main trucking cost.
LPG and fertiliser subsidies rise with energy prices.
Gas is the feedstock for urea and ammonia.
China uses ~55% of the world's copper.
China makes over half the world's steel; its exports set prices.
Chinese steel output sets iron ore demand.
China dominates aluminium supply and demand.
Data centres and grid upgrades are copper-intensive.
Raw-material costs pass through to steel.
Coking coal is the second main input.
RBI weighs global rates and the rupee.
Policy rate anchors the yield curve.
More government borrowing pushes yields up.
Global yields influence foreign demand for Indian bonds.
Bond prices fall when yields rise.
Rain-fed farming covers about half of cropland.
Spare cash goes to discretionary goods.
Earnings growth drives the index over time.
A strong dollar pulls money out of emerging markets.
Higher US yields make India relatively less attractive.
Foreign money flows to EMs when risk appetite is high.
Global EM fund flows include India.
Household money into SIPs and insurance.
Volatility rises when the market falls.
A wider deficit weakens the rupee.
Higher building costs raise home prices.
Peak demand raises exchange power prices.
Fast growth can store up future bad loans.
A healthy economy keeps borrowers paying.
Weddings and Dhanteras lift gold buying.
Two-wheelers and tractors depend on rural incomes.
Most vehicles are bought on loans.
US clients drive global IT budgets.

paints.name: Paints
drivers: Crude derivatives (solvents, monomers, binders) are the largest raw-material bucket; margins move with a 1–2 quarter lag.
Titanium dioxide is the main pigment cost.
Many inputs are imported or import-priced.
New homes and repainting drive decorative volumes.
Rural repainting follows farm incomes; heavy rains delay painting.
New competition (Birla Opus, JSW Paints) is pressuring share and pricing.
Higher rates cool housing and lower valuations of long-duration consumer stocks.
drives: Paint price hikes add to finishing costs for developers and households.

cement.name: Cement
drivers: Coal and pet coke fuel the kilns.
Diesel freight is a major cost.
Heavy rains halt construction in Jul–Sep.
drives: Cement price hikes raise building costs.

steel.name: Steel
drivers: Imported coking coal is the biggest cost.
Chinese exports set the global price floor.
Safeguard duties on imports protect prices.
drives: Body steel for autos and white goods.

zinc_silver.name: Zinc, lead & silver
drivers: Silver is a large profit contributor.

mining.name: Mining (coal, iron ore)
drivers: Price of e-auction coal and iron ore.

oil_upstream.name: Oil & gas producers
drives: Large dividend payer to the government.

oil_marketing.name: Oil refining & marketing
drivers: If pump prices are held, cheaper crude means bigger marketing margins.
Government asks them to absorb LPG losses.

refining_petchem.name: Refining & petrochemicals (diversified)
drivers: Refining margins (cracks) matter more than crude level.

gas_distribution.name: Gas transmission & city gas
drivers: Input cost for city gas; volume risk for transmission.
APM gas allocation and tariff orders.

power_utility.name: Power generation & utilities
drivers: Plant load factors and merchant prices.

power_equipment.name: Power & electrical equipment
drivers: Copper and steel are key inputs.

cables_wires.name: Cables & wires
drivers: Copper is ~70% of cost (passed on with a lag).

private_bank.name: Private banks
drivers: Rate cuts compress margins short-term but lift growth.
Lower bad loans mean lower provisions.

psu_bank.name: Public-sector banks
drivers: Large bond portfolios lose value when yields rise.
Bad-loan cycles hit PSU banks hardest.
drives: Biggest lenders to infrastructure and agriculture.

nbfc.name: NBFCs & consumer finance
drivers: They borrow from markets; costs follow yields.

housing_finance.name: Housing finance
drivers: Funding cost and loan demand both depend on rates.

gold_finance.name: Gold-loan companies
drivers: Higher gold prices raise loan sizes and collateral.
Borrowers are mostly rural and MSME.

insurance.name: Insurance
drivers: IRDAI rules on commissions and products.

capital_markets.name: AMCs, brokers & exchanges
drivers: Fees rise with market levels and activity.
SEBI curbs on F&O and fees.

it_services.name: IT services
drivers: ~60% of revenue comes from US clients.
A weaker rupee lifts rupee revenue and margins.
AI creates new work but can shrink some services.
drives: Salaries fund urban spending (Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad).

pharma.name: Pharmaceuticals
drivers: USFDA inspections and US drug pricing.
Many raw materials (APIs, KSMs) come from China.

fmcg_staples.name: FMCG staples (food, home & personal care)
drivers: Soaps and foods; India imports most edible oil.

tobacco.name: Cigarettes & diversified FMCG
drivers: Excise and GST hikes on cigarettes.

sugar_ethanol.name: Sugar & ethanol
drivers: Export quotas, ethanol pricing, cane prices.

agrochem.name: Agrochemicals
drivers: Sowing drives demand for crop protection.

fertiliser.name: Fertilisers
drives: Fertiliser subsidies are a large budget item.

specialty_chem.name: Specialty chemicals
drivers: US tariffs on China can shift orders to India.

auto_pv.name: Passenger vehicles
drivers: Running costs shift demand to CNG/EVs.

tyres.name: Tyres
drivers: Natural rubber is the largest input.
Synthetic rubber, carbon black and nylon are crude-derived.

jewellery.name: Jewellery & watches
drivers: Higher prices lift inventory gains and ticket sizes but cut grams sold.

construction_epc.name: Construction & engineering (EPC)
drivers: Steel and cement costs (often with escalation clauses).

defence.name: Defence & aerospace
drivers: Conflicts raise defence spending and export interest.

railways.name: Railways & rail equipment
drivers: Railway budget is the main driver.

logistics_ports.name: Logistics, ports & shipping
drivers: Red Sea disruptions raise freight rates.

telecom.name: Telecom
drivers: Tariff hikes lift revenue per user.

textiles.name: Textiles & apparel
drivers: US is the largest export market.
Exporters gain from a weaker rupee.
